findings.claim: Nelson Mandela, a Christian, spent 27 years in prison for opposing apartheid through protest rather than terrorism.
findings.truth: Mandela co-founded Umkhonto we Sizwe, the armed wing of the ANC, in 1961 and led its sabotage campaign; the Rivonia Trial convicted him of sabotage and conspiracy. The 27 years are right, but he cannot illustrate a paragraph arguing that faith inspires peace rather than violence. Replaced with Martin Luther King Jr, a Baptist minister jailed for non-violent protest.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Nelson Mandela and Rivonia Trial

findings.claim: Question 2 'Give two religious teachings about peace.' typed '1 mark - Give/Name', scheme '1 marks for each correct teaching, up to 2 marks ... [2 marks]'
findings.truth: Each theme is examined by one five-part question of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, marked out of 24. There is no 2-mark part; both short parts are single-point recall. Re-cut as a 1-mark 'give one' with a matching key.

findings.claim: 'The fuller seven-criteria version used today comes from the 1992 Catholic Catechism (CCC 2309), which added last resort, reasonable chance of success, proportional force, and civilian protection', repeated in the just war theory data-def as 'CCC 2309, seven criteria'.
findings.truth: Catechism 2309 gives four conditions: the damage must be lasting, grave and certain; all other means must have been shown impractical or ineffective; there must be serious prospects of success; and the use of arms must not produce evils graver than the evil removed. Protection of non-combatants is taught at 2313, not 2309, and no seven-criteria list appears in the Catechism.

findings.claim: many Muslims emphasise that Islam means “peace”
findings.truth: Islam means submission or surrender to God. It shares the Arabic root s-l-m with salaam, peace, which is why the two are linked, but the word itself does not mean peace. The 12-mark scheme in the same lesson uses the safer wording 'One meaning of Islam is peace' and is left alone.

findings.claim: Pope Francis has stated that “war is always a defeat for humanity”
findings.truth: The line is John Paul II's, from his address to the diplomatic corps on 13 January 2003. Francis has repeated it, usually crediting his predecessor. Re-attributed, with Francis's repetition kept.
findings.evidence: John Paul II, address to the diplomatic corps, 13 January 2003

findings.claim: Question 2 'Name two criteria of the just war theory.' typed '1 mark - Give/Name', scheme '1 marks for each correct criterion, up to 2 marks ... [2 marks]'
findings.truth: Same as F2: the short parts of the five-part question are worth 1 mark each and ask for one point.

findings.claim: 'If you have to respond to an attack, make your response proportionate' cited only as '(Qur'an)' in lesson 2 question 4 and again in lesson 3 content_html.
findings.truth: The quotation is Qur'an 16:126. The wording is accurate and the reference was simply missing; the 6-mark question credits a named source, so the chapter and verse are added.

findings.claim: Other religious organisations involved in supporting victims of war include Christian Aid, CAFOD (Catholic Agency for Overseas Development), and the Red Cross (founded on Christian principles of compassion).
findings.truth: The Red Cross is not a religious organisation. Henry Dunant's own faith moved him to found it, but the Movement is neutral and independent of any religion, and the Red Crescent and Red Crystal exist so the emblem carries no faith meaning. The theme requires one present-day RELIGIOUS organisation, so naming the Red Cross as one would cost marks. Replaced with Muslim Aid. Lesson 5 already lists the Red Cross as a secular body, so the unit also contradicted itself.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.1.4 'the work of one present day religious organisation'; ICRC on the emblem

findings.claim: Flashcard 4: 'The atomic bombs dropped on _____ and Nagasaki in 1945 killed over 200,000 people, many of them civilians' -> 'Hiroshima'
findings.truth: A single-word cloze harvested from a sentence, with no question form and no full stop. Re-cut as 'Which Japanese city, with Nagasaki, was destroyed by an atomic bomb in 1945?' The 200,000 figure itself is sound.
findings.evidence: house flashcard rules; casualty figure checked against standard estimates (about 140,000 Hiroshima, 70,000 Nagasaki by end 1945)

findings.claim: Flashcard 5: '_____ For and Against Nuclear Deterrence Arguments for deterrence: Nuclear weapons have arguably prevented major wars between nuclear powers since 1945' -> 'Arguments'
findings.truth: A broken cloze cut from a collapsible heading. The answer word 'Arguments' also appears inside its own question, so the card is unanswerable and teaches nothing. Replaced with a mutually assured destruction card, which the lesson content supports and which keeps all five answers in the deck unique.

findings.claim: “If you have to respond to an attack, make your response proportionate” (Qur'an 2:194) - in content_html and again in the mark schemes of questions 4 and 6.
findings.truth: That wording is Qur'an 16:126 ('If you retaliate, let it be equivalent to what you have suffered'). Qur'an 2:194 is a different verse ('if anyone attacks you, retaliate in the same manner'). A student who cites 2:194 for this quotation gives the wrong source in a question that credits a named source.

findings.claim: Question 2 'Give one reasons why some religious believers oppose weapons of mass destruction.' with the scheme 'One mark for each valid reason'
findings.truth: Ungrammatical stem, and the scheme implies more than one mark on a 1-mark part. Re-cut as 'Give one reason' with a 1-mark key.

findings.claim: Question 5 mark scheme: 'spelling/grammar: up to 5 additional marks.' and a band named 'Lower band (1-3)'.
findings.truth: This paper awards up to 3 marks for spelling, punctuation and grammar, on the 12-mark question. 96 marks plus 3 SPaG. Lessons 1 to 3 already say 3. The band name is also outside the house ladder; corrected to Low band.

findings.claim: For 5-mark questions, you must refer to scripture or sacred writings.
findings.truth: There is no 5-mark part. The five-part theme question is marked 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12, and the source-of-authority question in this very lesson is labelled 6 marks. The tip sent students to a question that does not exist.

findings.claim: “Making peace is better” (Surah 2) - in content_html, the exam tip, question 4's mark scheme and knowledge check 5's match pair.
findings.truth: 'Making peace is better' is the Hilali and Khan rendering of Qur'an 4:128. Surah 2 does not contain it. Reference corrected in all four places.
findings.evidence: quranx.com 4:128 translation list (Hilali & Khan: 'making peace is better')

findings.claim: The Arabic word “Islam” comes from “salam,” meaning peace or safety. Repeated in knowledge check 3 and question 4's mark scheme.
findings.truth: Islam means submission to God. It shares the root s-l-m with salam, peace, but does not come from it. The knowledge check even offered 'submission' as a distractor, so it trained the misconception directly; the stem is now about salam and the key stays 'peace'.

findings.claim: Question 2 'Give one ways in which religious believers help victims of war.' with the scheme 'Any two of the following, 1 mark each'
findings.truth: Ungrammatical stem, and the scheme asks for two answers on a 1-mark part. Re-cut as 'Give one way' with a 1-mark key.

findings.claim: Question 5 mark scheme opens 'Lower band (1-3)'.
findings.truth: Outside the house band ladder (Top / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Low). Renamed Low band.

findings.claim: Lesson 3 'Weapons of Mass Destruction & Peacemaking' and lesson 4 'Nuclear Weapons and Weapons of Mass Destruction' both teach what WMD are, the three types, nuclear deterrence and mutually assured destruction, and contrasting Christian and Muslim views on them. Lesson 5 then repeats lesson 3's peacemaking and victims-of-war material.
findings.truth: The spec bullet set is covered twice. Three options. (a) Leave both: the unit runs 5 lessons and students get a second pass, but the duplicate definitions, glossary entries and flashcards ('weapons of mass destruction', 'nuclear weapons', 'nuclear deterrence' appear in both decks with different wording) make revision noisy. (b) Narrow lesson 3 to peacemaking and religious responses to victims of war, and leave WMD wholly to lesson 4, which is the stronger WMD lesson (it has the Christian and Islamic teaching sections, Christian CND and the Utilitarian argument). (c) Merge 3 and 4 and drop to a 4-lesson unit, which would break narration, podcast and widget wiring. Recommendation: (b), as a content job, not a fact fix. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.1.4; the two lessons' own content

findings.claim: The 4-mark contrasting-beliefs question is set on forgiveness in lesson 1 and on peacemaking in lesson 5.
findings.truth: This theme requires contrasting beliefs on three issues only: violence, weapons of mass destruction and pacifism. Forgiveness is one of the three issues for the crime and punishment theme. Lessons 2, 3 and 4 already set this question on pacifism and WMD. Options: re-set lesson 1 question 3 on violence and lesson 5 question 3 on pacifism, so every 4-mark drill matches an issue the paper can set; or leave them as general practice. Recommendation: re-set them, as a content job on the next pass. Not edited.

findings.claim: Question type label '4 marks - Explain Similarities & Differences' in all five lessons, and lesson 1's exam tip naming 'the 4-mark “Explain similarities and differences” question'.
findings.truth: The paper sets either two similar or two contrasting beliefs, never both in one question, so the label names a question that does not exist. This is the corpus-wide question-type relabel queue, not a unit fix.

findings.claim: 'Utilitarians' is glossed, in the content data-def, the glossary and a flashcard, as 'An ethical theory that judges actions by whether they produce the greatest happiness for the greatest number of people.'
findings.truth: That defines Utilitarianism, not Utilitarians. The definition is correct in substance, so it costs no marks; it needs the term or the wording matching on the next content pass.

findings.claim: the Qur'an lists “the Merciful” and “the Compassionate” among the 99 names of Allah
findings.truth: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are both Qur'anic, but the Qur'an nowhere lists 99 names; the enumeration comes from hadith. 'Names the Merciful and the Compassionate' would be exact. Too small to be worth a narration re-run on its own.
findings.evidence: Qur'an 1:1-3; the list of 99 names is from Tirmidhi

findings.claim: The Prophet Muhammad said: “We have finished lesser jihad, let us now focus on greater jihad” (Hadith)
findings.truth: The greater jihad report is widely taught at GCSE but is graded weak by hadith scholars and is not in the canonical collections. The lesson labels it '(Hadith)' without a collection, which is the usual GCSE treatment, so it is left alone.
findings.evidence: standard hadith criticism of the 'greater jihad' report

findings.claim: Definition-front flashcards across lessons 1, 2, 3 and 5 carry a bare definition as the question, for example 'The absence of conflict and violence; a state of harmony between people or nations.' -> 'peace'.
findings.truth: These cards are correct and answerable but are not phrased as questions; the house form is 'Which word means ...?'. A corpus-wide flashcard form job, consistent with how the free-tier sibling unit was handled. Not edited.

summary: Scripture is otherwise sound: Matthew 5:9, 5:39, 5:44, 6:14, 22:39, 25:40, 26:52, Luke 23:34, Micah 6:8, Mark 12:31, 2 Corinthians 5:18-19 and Qur'an 2:190, 2:256, 5:8, 5:32, 6:151, 8:61, 22:39 and 42:40 all check out in a recognised translation with the right reference, and every knowledge-check key and match order is correct. The damage is concentrated in lessons 4 and 5, which were built to a different pattern from lessons 1 to 3: 'make your response proportionate' cited as Qur'an 2:194 instead of 16:126 three times, 'Making peace is better' cited as Surah 2 instead of 4:128 four times, a 5-mark question that this paper does not set, 5 SPaG marks where the paper gives 3, and 'Islam comes from salam meaning peace' taught as fact and drilled in a knowledge check. Lessons 1 to 3 repeat the free-tier sibling unit's faults (Mandela, Catechism 2309, the Red Cross as a religious organisation, two 2-mark questions) and add two broken flashcards in lesson 3.
